title: Uniform Completeness, Completion, and the Samuel Compactification

items.title: The Samuel uniformity generated by bounded uniformly continuous functions
Samuel function pseudometrics generate a uniformity coarser than the original one
items.strategy: For each uniformly continuous f:X-> [0,1], verify that p_f(x,y)=|f(x)-f(y)| is a pseudometric by the real absolute-value laws. Pull every p_f-ball back from the metric uniformity of [0,1]; finite intersections then show that the generated Samuel uniformity is coarser than the original uniformity.

items.title: The Samuel uniformity is totally bounded
items.strategy: Fix a basic entourage involving finitely many [0,1]-valued coordinates. Choose a finite small net in [0,1] for each coordinate, partition X into the finitely many nonempty coordinate cells, and use finite choice to select one representative from each cell. Treat the empty coordinate family and the empty space separately.

items.title: Assuming dependent choice, the Samuel uniformity induces the original topology
items.strategy: Coarsening gives one topological inclusion. For an original neighbourhood O of x, choose U[x] inside O, build a normal entourage sequence and its controlled pseudometric p, and use f(y)=min(1,4p(x,y)). The Samuel f-ball of radius one at x lies in O. Include the empty space explicitly.

items.title: The Samuel completion and, when compactifying, the Samuel compactification
Total boundedness passes to a uniform space with a dense uniformly continuous image
items.strategy: Given a target entourage, choose a symmetric entourage whose square is smaller and pull it back by uniform continuity. Cover the source by finitely many pulled-back balls. Density supplies a source image point near each target point, and a two-entourage composition puts that target point near the image of one of the finite source centres. Separate the empty target case.

items.title: Under the ultrafilter lemma the Samuel completion is compact, and under dependent choice plus the ultrafilter lemma it compactifies every separated uniform space
items.strategy: The Samuel uniformity is totally bounded, and the dense completion remains totally bounded. Completeness plus total boundedness gives compactness under the ultrafilter lemma. Under dependent choice the Samuel and original topologies agree; for a separated original uniformity this makes the completion map a topological embedding with dense image. With both choice principles it is therefore a compactification.

items.title: Under dependent choice and the ultrafilter lemma, uniformly continuous maps to compact Hausdorff spaces extend uniquely over the Samuel compactification
items.strategy: Give a compact Hausdorff target its unique compatible uniformity. Under dependent choice its topology is generated by the gauge of continuous [0,1]-valued functions. Composing those coordinate functions with the given uniformly continuous map shows that the map is uniformly continuous from the Samuel uniformity. Compactness makes the target complete, so the uniform-completion universal property gives the extension and density gives uniqueness.

items.title: Samuel compactifications are unique up to the unique isomorphism fixing the original space
items.strategy: Apply the compact-target extension property in both directions between two Samuel compactifications. The two composites agree with the identity on the dense original image, so uniqueness makes them identities.

items.title: Assuming dependent choice, a totally bounded uniformity equals its Samuel uniformity
items.strategy: For an original entourage U, construct a bounded controlled pseudometric p with a quarter-ball inside U. A finite p-net supplies finitely many distance functions f_z(y)=p(z,y). A sufficiently small simultaneous Samuel entourage for those functions forces p(x,y)<1/4 and hence lies in U. Combine this with the already proved coarsening and treat the empty space.

items.title: Under dependent choice the Samuel completion of a separated totally bounded space is its uniform completion; under the ultrafilter lemma it is compact
items.strategy: The preceding equality identifies the original and Samuel uniformities, so their Hausdorff completions are the same up to the unique uniform isomorphism fixing X. Under the ultrafilter lemma that completion is compact by completeness and total boundedness; keep this compactness clause separate from the DC identification.

items.title: Under dependent choice and the ultrafilter lemma, the Stone-Cech compactification maps continuously onto the Samuel compactification
items.strategy: A separated uniform space is Tychonoff under dependent choice, so use the evaluation-closure Stone-Cech compactification. Its universal property extends the Samuel compactification map. The image of the resulting map is compact and therefore closed in the Hausdorff Samuel compactification, while it contains the dense original image; hence it is onto.

title: Uniform Completeness, Completion, and the Samuel Compactification: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The Samuel compactification of a compact Hausdorff space adds no points
items.strategy: Use the unique compatible uniformity. Compactness gives completeness and total boundedness, so the identity is already a Hausdorff completion; the totally bounded agreement theorem identifies it with the Samuel compactification. Include the empty compact space.

items.title: The Samuel compactification of the open unit interval is the closed unit interval
items.strategy: Give (0,1) and [0,1] their usual metric uniformities. For epsilon>0 choose n>=2 with 1/n<epsilon; the finite grid {j/n:1<=j<n} is an epsilon-net in (0,1), as the integer-part lemma supplies the adjacent grid index. The inclusion has dense image and exactly pulls back the closed interval's uniformity, and compact [0,1] is complete and separated. Thus [0,1] is its Hausdorff uniform completion, and the totally bounded agreement theorem identifies the Samuel compactification.

items.title: The Samuel compactification of the discrete natural numbers is beta N
items.strategy: Define the discrete metric on N directly and verify its metric axioms. Its radius-1/2 entourage is the diagonal, so every map from this discrete uniformity is uniformly continuous. Hence the Samuel extension property and the Stone-Cech extension property quantify over the same maps into compact Hausdorff targets. Apply the two uniqueness arguments to identify the compactifications over N.

items.title: The Samuel compactification map need not be a uniform embedding for the original uniformity
items.strategy: Use the infinite discrete natural numbers and verify the discrete metric directly. Its radius-1/2 entourage balls are singletons, so a finite such ball cover would make N finite, contradicting the pigeonhole theorem. Thus the original uniformity is not totally bounded, while the Samuel uniformity is totally bounded. The completion map pulls back precisely the Samuel uniformity, so it cannot also pull back the strictly finer original discrete uniformity. Distinguish this from its being a topological embedding under dependent choice.

items.title: The Samuel reflection of a nonempty indiscrete uniform space is a singleton
items.strategy: For the indiscrete uniformity {X x X}, uniform continuity into [0,1] forces every Samuel coordinate function to be constant. The generated Samuel uniformity is therefore indiscrete, its separated quotient identifies every pair of points, and its Hausdorff completion is the one-point space.
